additions.name: GPT Researcher
additions.description: Open-source autonomous agent that plans sub-questions, runs parallel web/document searches, and compiles a cited research report on a query you supply; has a companion MCP server (gptr-mcp).
additions.notes: ~29k GitHub stars, Apache 2.0, active commits through 2026, ranked #1 on the CMU DeepResearchGym benchmark at time of review; still an LLM pipeline so verify every cited claim against the source it links, not the summary text.

additions.name: Open Deep Research (LangChain)
additions.description: Configurable open-source deep-research agent that plans, searches (Tavily or MCP-connected sources), compresses findings, and writes a sourced report; runnable locally via LangGraph Studio.
additions.notes: 12,678 stars, MIT, benchmarked on Deep Research Bench; GitHub currently lists repo status as ARCHIVED even though commit history is recent through mid-2026, so confirm active maintenance before relying on it for ongoing work.

additions.name: osint-mcp-server (badchars)
additions.description: MCP server exposing 37 tools across 12 OSINT sources (Shodan, VirusTotal, Censys, SecurityTrails, DNS, WHOIS/RDAP, certificate transparency, BGP, Wayback Machine, GeoIP) to any MCP-compatible AI agent.
additions.notes: 21 of 37 tools work with no API key; the rest need free-tier keys for Shodan/VirusTotal/SecurityTrails/Censys. Created March 2026, 47 stars/0 open issues at review time — the MCP-OSINT-server space overall is young and thinly adopted, so treat any single server as a convenience wrapper around the underlying APIs, not an independent authority.

additions.name: Picarta
additions.description: AI image-geolocation service that estimates where an outdoor photo was taken from visual content alone (no EXIF/GPS required), returning coordinates with a confidence score.
additions.notes: Markets directly to OSINT investigators/journalists/law enforcement. Treat output as a lead, not a finding: AI geolocation models are known to be confidently wrong on generic or indoor scenes and should be cross-checked against landmarks, signage, vegetation, and satellite imagery before being cited.

additions.name: GeoSpy
additions.description: AI photo-geolocation tool used by law-enforcement/enterprise customers, claiming meter-level accuracy from image content; access is sales-gated rather than self-serve.
additions.notes: No public self-serve tier; requires contacting sales, so most independent investigators cannot test its accuracy claims directly. "Meter-level accuracy" and "10,000+ cases" are vendor-stated, not independently benchmarked at time of review — cross-check any result against manual landmark analysis.

additions.name: Hugging Face Hub (Models)
additions.description: Searchable public catalog of 15,000+ machine-learning models with model cards documenting architecture, training data, license, and known limitations — used to trace provenance of a model or fine-tune.
additions.notes: Model card quality and license accuracy are self-reported by uploaders; useful as a first stop for provenance but not a verified registry.

additions.name: Epoch AI Data
additions.description: Free, actively updated dataset and dashboards tracking notable AI models, training compute, data centers, chip sales, and AI-company financials, licensed CC-BY for reuse.
additions.notes: Independent research org (Epoch AI); good for cross-checking vendor claims about training compute or release timelines.

additions.name: AI Incident Database
additions.description: Crowd-curated, searchable database of real-world incidents where deployed AI systems caused or nearly caused harm, indexed by system, developer, and incident type.
additions.notes: Entries are submitted/reviewed by a community and vary in depth; use as a lead generator and verify each incident against its cited primary source.

additions.name: AIAAIC Repository
additions.description: Independent repository logging AI, algorithmic, and automation incidents and controversies worldwide, alongside separate catalogs of AI systems and training datasets.
additions.notes: Non-profit-run and updated with new 2026 entries at time of review; broader scope than incidentdatabase.ai (also tracks systems/datasets), so the two complement rather than duplicate each other.

additions.name: GPTZero
additions.description: AI-generated text detector that scores a submitted document or pasted text for likelihood of being LLM-written, with a mixed-text mode for documents combining human and AI writing.
additions.notes: Vendor claims ~99% accuracy; the independent RAID benchmark put detection at ~95.7% with ~1% false positives on human text, but accuracy drops on paraphrased or heavily edited AI text and rises again on outputs from newer, less-filtered models — treat a single score as suggestive, never as proof, and never as the sole basis for an accusation.

additions.name: Hive Moderation (AI-Generated Content Detection)
additions.description: Multimodal classifier that flags AI-generated or AI-edited text, images, video, and audio, aimed at trust-and-safety and content-verification workflows.
additions.notes: Vendor claims >99% accuracy; independent tests found accuracy ranging roughly 94-98% depending on generator and content type, with false positives on heavily processed, HDR, or AI-upscaled real photos. Detection is defeated by adversarial signature-removal tools (e.g. so-called 'Undetectr') and degrades against newer image/video generators — state findings as probabilistic, never as confirmation.

additions.name: Content Credentials Verify (C2PA)
additions.description: Drag-and-drop tool that reads and displays C2PA Content Credentials metadata embedded in an image, video, or document, showing edit history and generative-AI disclosures when present.
additions.notes: Coverage is still rolling out across cameras, editing tools, and generators — the absence of a Content Credential is NOT evidence that content is unedited or not AI-generated, only that no participating tool signed it.

additions.name: LMArena (Chatbot Arena)
additions.description: Live, crowdsourced leaderboard ranking large language models by blind pairwise human preference votes (Bradley-Terry/Elo-style rating with confidence intervals).
additions.notes: Measures aggregate stylistic preference from public votes, NOT factual accuracy, safety, or task-specific correctness; rankings near the top often sit within overlapping confidence intervals and the site itself warns prompts may be used for provider evaluation and shared publicly — do not cite a high rank as proof a model is more reliable or more truthful.

additions.name: Perplexity Deep Research
additions.description: Deep-research mode that runs dozens of iterative searches, reads source documents, and produces a written report with inline citations to the pages it used.
additions.notes: Cites its sources, unlike a plain chatbot, but is a proprietary closed system — verify each cited claim against the linked source rather than trusting the synthesis, and note that free-tier query limits apply.

additions.name: Vane (formerly Perplexica)
additions.description: Self-hosted, open-source AI search engine that answers a query with inline citations by combining a local/hosted LLM with a bundled SearxNG metasearch backend.
additions.notes: Renamed from Perplexica to Vane in March 2026 (same underlying project/codebase); self-hosting avoids sending queries to a third party, but result quality depends entirely on the LLM and search backend you configure.

additions.name: Dutch National Algorithm Register
additions.description: Official Dutch government registry publishing descriptions of algorithms and AI systems used by public-sector bodies, including purpose, data used, and risk classification.
additions.notes: Live registry listing 1,538 algorithms at time of review; coverage depends on individual agencies actually registering their systems, so absence from the register does not mean a public body isn't using an algorithm.

additions.name: Odap — Observatoire des algorithmes publics
additions.description: French civil-society inventory documenting AI and algorithmic systems used by French public administrations, including funding, evaluation status, and legal-compliance gaps.
additions.notes: Volunteer-run and explicitly non-exhaustive (120 systems documented in its Nov 2025 edition); it reports 18 of 24 legally-obligated systems were non-compliant with French transparency law, illustrating how incomplete official self-disclosure can be.

changes.name: Manus
changes.detail: Meta acquired the Chinese-founded agentic-AI platform for $2B in Dec 2025; China's NDRC ordered the deal unwound in Apr 2026 over foreign-investment rules, Meta cut Manus off from its internal systems in June 2026 and required deletion of user data created since 29 Dec 2025 by 24 Aug 2026, and Manus is reverting to independent operation.
changes.notes: Directory should flag this as an unstable/high-churn agentic tool rather than a dependable long-term OSINT resource.

changes.name: Yupp
changes.detail: Crowdsourced AI-model comparison/leaderboard service (1.3M users, $33M a16z-crypto seed) shut down on 31 Mar 2026, citing failure to reach product-market fit as agentic AI systems evolved.

changes.name: Perplexica
changes.detail: Self-hosted open-source citing AI search engine renamed to Vane in March 2026; same codebase and repository.
